newsitem.title: UK: Ldn Freight - Capers seen easing, BFI off 20.
newsitem.headline: Ldn Freight - Capers seen easing, BFI off 20.

text.p: LONDON, Jan 22 (reuter) - The BFI fell 20 points to 1435

with brokers speculating that the Caper market was now beginning to ease in the Atlantic. Fewer Panamax fixtures were reported but at best these were marginally lower and at worst quite significantly weaker. Handy-size grain fixtures in the Atlantic continued at poor levels. Bad weather is still disrupting shipping programmes in the northern hemisphere.

Two more stems of 52/54,000 heavy grain were said to have been booked overnight for first half Ffeb, for account of HMM nd Hanjin, at $23.95 no combo each, 5 cents down on yesterday's rates. Geepee were reported to have taken a Panamax on subjects from US Gulf for grain to Red Sea or MidEast Gulf, and Iranian charterers fixed New Paloma 69,417 dwt for grain from the EU to Iran at $26.00. Capt John 163,920 dwt, Mehmet Bey 68,789 dwt and Pacific Nova 69,073 dwt were all rumoured fixed from US Gulf to the Far East, not necessarily in grain, but details were lacking.

Another dismal rate was seen in the handy-size sector with Dreyfus booking United Purpose for 40,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Huelva-Barcelona range for Jan/Feb at $13.60. It was rumoured Dreyfus also fixed 30,000 grain Brazil/Continent at only $15.00. New chartering enquiry today included K Line with 52/54,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan for Feb 10/20, Continental 50,000 meals US Gulf/Qingdao Feb 3/7, Mid-South Feeds 1.3/1m cft delivery Mississippi Feb 5/15 trip Red Sea, Andre 15,000 heavy grain and 5,000 meals US Gulf/Leixoes Jan 27/Feb 5, and Glencore 25,000 sbm pellets up River/Portugal for prompt/Feb 5.
A number of Capers were fixed at steady levels but brokers were generally agreed that so far this week was relatively quiet with the possibility of a weaker trend developing in the Alantic.

Courageous 149,190 dwt was said to have fixed and failed delivery Passero end March for srt period at $15,500 daily, Docecape 151,852 dwt was also booked privately from Passero, and the 1973-built Orfeas 120,144 dwt was believed fixed by Deiulemar for Norfolk/Constanza coal for mid Feb in the region of $7.25/7.50. Klaveness fixed the 1972-built Larina for 155,000 ironore Pt Cartier/Fos for Feb/March at a weaker $7.50, and brokers speculated that this vessel was being manoeuvred into a position to be sold for scrap. British Steel were said to have fixed ironore on Baron Bay 149,2 dwt on timecharter from Nouadhibou to Port Talbot but details were not released.
In the Panamax category coal business was believed fixed

by Seatrans Richards Bay/Lisbon (possibly at about $7.50), and by Goldbeam Richrds Bay/Le hHvre, and brokers reported weaker conditions in this area. Konpolis 78,573 dwt was rumoured fixed for coal Davant/Tragona by enemm at $9.25. Deiulemar booked a 1974-built 54,100 dwt vessel delivery Rotterdam for 2 laden legs Atlantic Minerals trading at $6,000 daily. Fertilizer charterers were active but brokers said that Seyang's fixture of the 1975-built Menalon 65,400 dwt, ballasting from the Far East which agreed $12,000 daily plus $220,000 bonus delivery Tampa end Jan trip China, had failed.

HANDY SIZES Ekaterina a 35,982 dwt was fixed by OK shipping for scrap from the Continent to Turkey at $9,000 daily and Clipper took the 1974-built Tomahawk 34,000 dwt delivery La Plata trip US Gulf at close to $6,800 daily.
